finding.title: Growth tilt NaN boost silently destroys valid predictions for newly listed names
finding.problem: apply_growth_tilt computes boost_values = boost_w * (tilt_signal - 0.5) * 2 and applies it with `adjusted[valid_mask] = predictions[valid_mask] + boost_values[valid_mask]`. Unlike apply_pead_boost (which does `.fillna(0.0)` on its boost term), the boost is never NaN-filled, and pandas boolean-mask assignment propagates RHS NaN into mask-True cells (verified empirically on the venv's pandas 3.0.2: a valid prediction 1.0 with NaN boost becomes NaN). tilt_signal is NaN wherever ANY leg is NaN: the fundamental leg needs eps_raw.shift(252) (252 trading rows of BEST_EPS) and the revision leg needs rolling(63, min_periods=21) of cleaned revisions. With listing_mask_enabled ON (production data-accuracy layer), UniverseData pins every sheet to NaN pre-listing (data_loader.py:1090-1099), so a newly listed name has NaN fundamentals until listing+252 trading days — its valid model predictions are silently converted to NaN and optimize_portfolio then treats the name as invalid alpha (mu=0, pinned to bm weight, portfolio_optimizer.py:317/701). This contradicts the function's own 'preserve NaN structure' comment.
finding.scenario: Production run (growth_tilt_enabled=true, listing_mask_enabled ON, 250 universe): TKO lists 2023-09. From listing+~1 day the model scores it (features are median-imputed), but BEST_EPS.shift(252) is NaN until ~2024-09, so fund_composite -> tilt_signal -> boost is NaN and TKO's prediction is set to NaN at every rebalance for ~1 year: the name can never receive active weight, silently. Same for HWM post-2020-04, SNDK 2025-02, and every listing_dates entry; a ticker entirely absent from the Factset_EPS_Revision sheet is zapped permanently.
finding.fix: In apply_growth_tilt, change `boost_values = boost_w * tilt_centered` to `boost_values = (boost_w * tilt_centered).fillna(0.0)` (mirrors the apply_pead_boost NaN-preserving idiom). Note: this is a production-number-changing fix — gate via the decision log per CLAUDE.md §8 before flipping.

In production (listing_mask_enabled=True, config.py:118; growth_tilt_enabled=True, weight 0.25, config.py:517-520), data_loader.py:1090-1099 re-masks every per-ticker sheet to NaN pre-listing, so each of the ~34 config.listing_dates names (config.py:138-176: TKO 2023-09-12, HWM 2020-04-01, WDC/SNDK 2025-02-24, COF 2025-05-19, ARM, CEG, PLTR, GEV/GE, RDDT, SNOW, APP, ABNB, DASH, RBLX, UMG, BN, 285A, ...) has NaN tilt for ~252 trading days post-listing while predict_cross_sectional (model_trainer.py:510-558) DOES score it from listing+1 (prediction-level mask at backtest.py:1882-1890 runs before overlays; growth tilt at 1911 then NaNs the valid score). Severity stays high (silent, production-ON overlay, contradicts its own comment, suppresses the newly-listed segment, ~20+ name-year windows baked into the S0(250) baseline) rather than critical (bounded effect: names are bm-pinned, not corrupted; no window is active on the live book as of 2026-08-27). Production impact stays changes_production_numbers: the current baseline numbers include the effect and any future listing re-activates it.

finding.title: Factor features are literal 0.0 on US holidays and lagging tail dates (empirically confirmed on 119 production dates)
finding.problem: build_factor_features builds every fac_* feature on common_dates = data.dates.intersection(factor_ret.index) and never forward-fills to the universe calendar. The universe calendar (intersection of per-ticker sheets, which are ffill-imputed dense) includes US market holidays and tail dates where Factor_PX_LAST has no row. In assembly.build_all_features those dates reindex to NaN, the per-date cross-sectional median of a broadcast feature is then NaN for all 250 tickers, and the final fillna(0.0) writes literal zeros. Because Factor-group features skip the CS z-score, the model receives raw-value zeros: fac_yield_slope=0 falsely asserts a flat curve (sign-flipping the signal throughout the 2022-23 inversion), and fac_F_Quality/Growth/Value_mom_63d and fac_value_growth_63d falsely assert neutral factor momentum. Verified against the production pickle: exactly 119 of 3,283 dates have ALL five whitelisted fac_* features == 0.0, and the dates are precisely US holidays (Presidents Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, July 4, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year, MLK) plus 2026-08-25 — a normal Tuesday, i.e. a tail date where the factor sheet lagged PX_LAST. regime.py handles the identical gap correctly with .reindex(dates).ffill(); factor.py does not.
finding.scenario: Every US-holiday date (~9-11/year) is a training ranking query in which all 250 stocks carry corrupted macro conditioning, mis-routing conditioning splits in rank_xendcg trees. Worse operationally: on 2026-08-25 (confirmed) the live prediction/expected-rebalance path ran with fac_yield_slope=0 instead of the true slope; prediction_ema_alpha=0.5 then bleeds the corrupted prediction into subsequent days, and a 21-day rebalance landing on/after such a date trades on it.
finding.fix: In bcast (factor.py:25-27), compute the feature on the factor calendar as today but return it reindexed to the full universe calendar with forward fill: vals = series.reindex(data.dates).ffill().values..., index=data.dates — mirroring regime.py's established idiom. Leading warm-up NaN behavior is unchanged. Note: this changes certified production numbers, so it must go through the decision-log gate (S0 re-certification) rather than a silent patch.

verdict.corrected_detail: CONFIRMED, with every sub-claim independently reproduced. Mechanism: src/features/factor.py:23 builds common_dates = data.dates.intersection(factor_ret.index), and bcast (lines 25-27) returns frames indexed only on common_dates with no ffill to the universe calendar. Upstream, data_loader.py load_factor_sheets (lines 756-777) ffills only on the factor sheet's own row index, and lines 1256-1258 subset it to the intersection with self.dates - so universe-calendar dates absent from the raw Factor_PX_LAST/Factor_Returns sheets (US market closures, and tail dates where the factor sheet lags PX_LAST) never enter factor_ret.index. Empirical reproduction on the production S0(250) baseline pickle outputs/s14_overlay_base_250/backtest_result.pkl (panel 3,283 dates x 250 tickers x 65 features): exactly 119/3,283 dates have all five whitelisted fac_* features (fac_yield_slope, fac_F_Quality/Growth/Value_mom_63d, fac_value_growth_63d) == 0.0 for every ticker; the dates are precisely US closures (MLK, Presidents Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth from 2022, July 4, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year, plus special closures 2018-12-05 and 2025-01-09) plus 2026-08-25, a normal Tuesday that is the panel's last date (factor sheet ended 08-24 while PX_LAST tail-extended to 08-25). Sign-flip verified: fac_yield_slope -0.7846 (2022-11-23) -> 0.0000 (2022-11-24) -> -0.7750 (2022-11-25); 14 corrupted dates inside the 2022-07..2023-12 inversion era where the median true slope was -0.548; 2026-08-25 shows 0.0 vs +0.4645 the prior day. No downstream guard exists: r.predictions contains full 250 non-null predictions on all corrupted dates including 2026-08-25, so these dates are live training ranking queries and prediction dates, and the corrupted final date is exactly what the daily batch/expected-rebalance what-if path consumes, with prediction_ema_alpha=0.5 bleeding it into subsequent days. The proposed fix (reindex to data.dates + ffill inside bcast, mirroring regime.py) is correct and must go through S0 re-certification per the decision-log gate since it changes the certified production panel.

finding.title: risk.json covariance uses imputed data.returns, not production's raw_returns risk source
finding.problem: The risk.json block builds its covariance from `data.returns` (the dense, imputed USD P&L panel), but the production optimizer estimates covariance from `data.raw_returns` (un-imputed, pre-listing-masked; backtest.py:1989-1991 -> risk_source at 1432 -> hist at 1538). data_loader.py explicitly documents this split ("공분산 경로는 별도의 마스킹된 raw_returns를 쓴다"). Worse, estimate_covariance (portfolio_optimizer.py:84-93) switches estimator families on NaN presence: raw_returns windows contain NaN (pre-listing names, missing days) so production uses the pairwise-covariance path, while the dense export panel goes through LedoitWolf. The same wrong source is used in the monitoring.json TE-constraint audit loop (line 1640), whose docstring claims it recomputes "the optimizer's ex-ante TE ... using the same trailing covariance window". The exporter's own expected_rebalance block (lines 1891-1898) uses raw_returns, confirming the intended source.
finding.scenario: At a rebalance date where any of the 250 names has NaN in the trailing 126-day raw-returns window (always true post-S14 with masked entrants like TKO pre-2023-09), production estimated Sigma via pairwise covariance on masked data while risk.json/monitoring recompute LedoitWolf on imputed data. The exported estimated_tracking_error, name/sector active-risk shares, headroom, and `estimated_te_breached`/`te_constraint_breached` flags then differ from what the optimizer actually enforced; a spurious `estimated_te_breached=true` propagates into validate_portfolio_bundles.evaluate_production and flips the dashboard registry status to HOLD (or masks a real breach).
finding.fix: In both blocks, mirror the expected_rebalance source selection: `risk_source = getattr(data, 'raw_returns', None); risk_source = risk_source.reindex(index=data.returns.index, columns=tickers) if isinstance(risk_source, pd.DataFrame) else data.returns[tickers]` and slice hist windows from it (line 1526 and line 1640).

verdict.corrected_detail: CONFIRMED with two refinements. (A) Source mismatch verified: risk.json builds its covariance from the imputed dense panel data.returns (scripts/export_operating_data.py:1526) and the monitoring.json TE-constraint audit does the same (:1640), while production estimates covariance from the un-imputed, pre-listing-masked data.raw_returns (src/backtest.py:1989-1991 -> risk_source :1432 -> hist window :1538 -> estimate_covariance :2059). data_loader.py:1476-1483 documents the split ("공분산 경로는 별도의 마스킹된 raw_returns"); estimate_covariance (portfolio_optimizer.py:84-93) switches estimator family on NaN presence (pairwise vs LedoitWolf), so masked raw windows and imputed dense windows diverge structurally, not just numerically. The exporter's own expected_rebalance block uses raw_returns (:1891-1898), confirming intent. Empirical proof from shipped artifacts: the production bundle's monitoring.json contains 5 tracking_error_constraint rows with breached=true (2020-05-07..2020-12-29, max estimated_te 0.038695 vs the 0.035 cap the optimizer enforces as a hard constraint in both MVO and projection) — impossible if the audit used the optimizer's Sigma; and the challenger bundle (iter15, optvol OFF, cap 0.045) shows 6 rows sitting EXACTLY at 0.045 at 2025-26 dates whose trailing raw windows are NaN-free — sources coincide precisely when no NaN exists, diverge otherwise. Propagation verified: risk.json guardrails -> validate_portfolio_bundles.py:492/:505 -> evaluate_production :591 -> fail-closed HOLD :607; the current live registry HOLD is in fact driven by top_name (0.418) / top_sector (0.937) active-risk shares computed from this same wrong-source Sigma. Refinement 1: the scenario's "always true post-S14" overstates NaN presence — windows after ~mid-2025 (126 trading days past the last masked entrant, SNDK 2025-02) can be NaN-free, and there the sources provably agree (exact-at-cap challenger rows); the estimator-family divergence holds for the large majority of historical audit rows (any window overlapping TKO pre-2023-09, HWM pre-2020-04, PLTR pre-2020-09, GEV, SNDK, etc.). Refinement 2: the finding names only one of two mechanisms — the risk.json (:1527) and monitoring (:1643-1650) blocks ALSO omit the S13.41 option-vol diagonal scaling that production applies (option_vol_covariance_enabled: true in codex_causal_rank_65.yaml; backtest.py:2062-2065), so the observed production-bundle divergence is the joint effect of both; the expected_rebalance block handles both correctly (:1891-1910) and a faithful fix should mirror both, not just the returns source.

Code trace: production covariance comes from raw_returns (masked, un-imputed) via backtest.py:1989->1432->1538->estimate_covariance, while export_operating_data.py:1526 and :1640 feed the imputed dense data.returns into the same estimator; portfolio_optimizer.py:84-93 then routes the two sources through different estimator families (pairwise vs LedoitWolf) whenever the raw window has NaN, which is guaranteed for any window overlapping a masked entrant's pre-listing period (most of 2018-2025). Decisive empirical evidence, obtained without running any backtest: (1) the production bundle's TE audit reports 5 breaches of a hard optimizer constraint (max 0.038695 vs 0.035) — mathematically impossible under the optimizer's actual Sigma, so the audit is provably recomputing with a different covariance despite its docstring claiming "the same trailing covariance window"; (2) the challenger bundle (no optvol, cap 0.045) shows 6 rows exactly at the cap to 6 decimals at 2025-26 dates where raw windows are NaN-free — exact reproduction of the binding constraint happens precisely when the two sources coincide, corroborating the mechanism from the null side. The HOLD-propagation path in the scenario is real (risk.json guardrails -> _risk_guardrails -> evaluate_production, fail-closed), and the live registry's current HOLD is driven by name/sector risk shares computed from the same wrong-source Sigma. Severity stays high within its ops scope: the artifact's stated purpose (auditing the optimizer's ex-ante TE constraint) is structurally unfulfilled, it already ships false breach rows, and its flags feed the fail-closed production HOLD gate the team uses for governance — it can both fabricate and mask breaches. Production impact stays ops_or_test_only: the exporter never feeds back into the optimizer, backtest, or reported performance numbers; only monitoring/dashboard/registry status is affected.

finding.title: risk.json and monitoring TE audit omit the production option-IV covariance diagonal scaling
finding.problem: Production has option_vol_covariance_enabled=true (codex_causal_rank_65.yaml, S13.41): the loop scales Sigma as diag(s) @ cov @ diag(s) before both MVO and projection (backtest.py:2058-2065), so the 0.035 ex-ante TE cap is enforced on the scaled Sigma. The risk.json block (line 1527) and the per-rebalance TE-constraint audit in monitoring.json (lines 1643-1663) call estimate_covariance without the optvol scaling and then compare the resulting TE against te_limit=0.035, contradicting the audit's stated method. The exporter demonstrably knows how to apply it — the expected_rebalance path does (lines 1900-1910, applied inside build_expected_rebalance at 765-771).
finding.scenario: The optimizer binds the TE cap at 0.035 under the IV-scaled Sigma. On a date where IV scaling shrinks stressed-name variances (its normal effect), the unscaled-LW TE recomputed by the audit reads above 0.035 -> te_constraint_rows mark `breached=true`, monitoring guardrails report te_constraint_breach_count>0 and risk.json can report estimated_te_breached=true -> production HOLD status in the registry, all while the hard constraint was actually satisfied at every rebalance.
finding.fix: After estimating cov in both blocks, apply the same diagonal scaling when cfg.option_vol_covariance_enabled: build/reuse the optvol scale panel (as done at lines 1900-1910) and do `cov = np.diag(s) @ cov @ np.diag(s)` with the scale row at the audited date before computing TE/risk contributions.

Mechanism verified end-to-end: production variant codex_causal_rank_65.yaml:143 has option_vol_covariance_enabled=true; estimate_covariance (src/portfolio_optimizer.py:73-124) does not apply the S13.41 scaling internally — src/backtest.py:2059-2065 applies diag(s)@cov@diag(s) after the call, and the projection reuses the identical scaled matrix via diagnostics["cov_matrix"] (backtest.py:2080-2081, 1613-1638), so the hard TE cap quad_form(active,cov)<=0.035^2/252 (portfolio_optimizer.py:321-324) is enforced on the scaled Sigma at both MVO and projection. The risk.json block (scripts/export_operating_data.py:1527, feeding estimated_te_breached at :1578) and the per-rebalance TE audit (:1643-1650, breached rows at :1662, count at :1664/:1713-1715) both call estimate_covariance without the scaling and compare against te_limit=cfg.max_te_annual=0.035, while the same file's expected_rebalance path does apply it (:1900-1910 -> build_expected_rebalance :765-771; shipped bundle confirms option_vol_cov_scaling_applied=true). The predicted false-positive symptom is already present in the shipped production artifact: outputs/operating_codex_causal_rank_65/monitoring.json has 5 rows breached=true (2020-05-07 0.0354, 2020-06-05 0.0387, 2020-07-06 0.0363, 2020-08-04 0.0377, 2020-12-29 0.0364 vs limit 0.035) while optimizer_failure_rate=0.0 and solver_fallback_rate=0.0 — impossible as genuine ex-ante breaches under the enforced hard constraint; they are audit-Sigma artifacts. HOLD linkage confirmed: validate_portfolio_bundles.py:492/505 feeds risk.json guardrails into evaluate_production (:590-607), whose estimated_te_ok check binds on estimated_te_breached; latest headroom is 0.0032 vs historical audit divergence up to +0.004, so a false HOLD is one near-cap rebalance away. Corrections: (1) the audit blocks additionally use data.returns while the production loop uses data.raw_returns as risk source (backtest.py:1432, 1989-1991) — a second, unnamed Sigma mismatch; the fix should align both. (2) monitoring's te_constraint_breach_count does NOT feed the HOLD gate — only risk.json's latest-date estimated_te_breached does, and evaluate_production is report-only (never blocks validation), so the scenario slightly overstates the breach-count->HOLD path. finding.title: listing_meta_columns precedence inverted: last column wins, not first
finding.problem: resolve_listing_dates iterates config.listing_meta_columns in order ['Eligibility_Start_Date', 'Listing_Date', 'IPO_Date', 'First_Trade_Date'] and unconditionally overwrites resolved[ticker] on every matching column (line 552). The list reads as a priority order (most-specific continuity date first), but the loop gives the LAST-listed generic column final say: a First_Trade_Date/IPO_Date value silently overrides an Eligibility_Start_Date continuity date. Verified against the live workbook: Universe_Meta currently has only [Name, Sector, Status] columns, so no meta column matches today and the path is dormant (all sources are px_last_inferred/config_override).
finding.scenario: A future workbook refresh adds both Eligibility_Start_Date (e.g. a spin/merger continuity date like GEV 2024-04-02) and IPO_Date/First_Trade_Date (the original listing, years earlier) to Universe_Meta for a name that is NOT in config.listing_dates. The loop resolves the eligibility date to the original IPO date, un-masking the predecessor-entity history (exactly the TKO/WWE, HWM/Arconic class of live-ghost data the mask exists to block) — pre-continuity rows silently enter the training panel, features, and cap-weighted benchmark with no error.
finding.fix: Make the first-listed column authoritative: iterate `for configured_name in reversed(getattr(config, "listing_meta_columns", [])):` (so earlier-listed columns overwrite later ones), or skip a ticker already resolved by a higher-priority meta column. config.listing_dates overrides still run last and stay authoritative either way.

finding.title: Trailing-IC confidence consumes unmatured (future-return) ICs when rebalance_freq < forward_horizon
finding.problem: simulate_portfolio appends IC at each rebalance date s as corr(pred(s), targets.loc[s]) where target(s) = cum[s+20]/cum[s]-1 (target_engine.py:37) — realized only at s+20. The next rebalance at s+freq reads `recent_ics = ic_values[-trailing_ic_window:]` into compute_signal_confidence, which scales eta and the no-trade band, i.e. it changes traded weights. If freq < forward_horizon (20), the most recent IC entries embed returns that have not yet been realized at decision time — direct lookahead into position sizing. Production (freq=21) is safe by exactly one day, but simulate_portfolio's own signature default is rebalance_freq=10, and faster-rebalance experiments (e.g. the §S13.40 10BD arm) silently ran with this leak.
finding.scenario: Any caller invoking simulate_portfolio with rebalance_freq<=19 (including the function's own default 10): at rebalance t, ic_values[-1] is the IC from t-10 whose target spans t-10..t+10 — 10 days of future returns leak into confidence -> eta -> weights, inflating the arm's measured IR versus a causal implementation.
finding.fix: Record each IC with its maturity index (s + effective_label_horizon(config)) and filter `recent_ics` to entries matured strictly before t_idx (or simply shift consumption by ceil(horizon/freq) entries). Byte-identical at freq=21 given horizon 20 if the filter is maturity_idx <= t_idx.

finding.title: mom_accel_63_252 partial-window sum (min_periods=126) fabricates +2σ momentum-acceleration for newly listed names (TKO confirmed)
finding.problem: build_lean_momentum_composites computes mom252 = returns.rolling(252, min_periods=126).sum() but mom63 with min_periods=63 (full). cs_rank then compares a 126-150-day partial return SUM for recently listed (listing-masked) names against genuine 252-day sums for the rest of the universe. finding.title: Revision spike cleaner only delays persistent rollover artifacts by one day instead of removing them
finding.problem: clean_revision_spikes masks the transition day t (cleaned[combined]=NaN then ffill restores the pre-spike level for day t only), but the spike masks are computed from daily_diff of the ORIGINAL series. For a Factset rollover that re-baselines and persists (e.g. 80 → 5 and stays 5), day t+1's original diff is 0, so t+1 is never masked and the cleaned stream reads ..., 80(t), 5(t+1): the full −75 artificial step enters the cleaned series one day late. Consequently the production features eps_rev, eps_rev_ma_63d, eps_rev_trend, sales_rev_ma_63d — and the PEAD/growth-tilt overlays that consume the same get_cleaned_revision stream — still absorb nearly the full rollover artifact; only single-day V-shaped spikes are genuinely cleaned. The printed 'down-spikes=N' counters overstate the cleaning actually achieved, and the docstring's stated purpose ('직전 정상값 복원') is not met for the persistent case, which is the dominant rollover shape.
finding.scenario: reversion_gated (production mode): stock with eps_rev 80 rolls to a new consensus period at 5. Day t is masked to 80; day t+1 is 5. eps_rev_diff_5d at t+1 ≈ −75, eps_rev_ma_63d absorbs the artificial level shift, and the PEAD/growth-tilt overlays tilt the score on a data artifact — exactly what the cleaner exists to prevent, merely one day later.
finding.fix: After masking day t, extend the mask forward while the original series remains collapsed relative to the pre-spike level (e.g. keep masking while |orig − prev_normal| > threshold and |orig| < |prev_normal|·reversion_ratio), or equivalently re-run spike detection on the cleaned stream so the reappearing step at t+1 trips the same gate. Any change alters the certified baseline and needs the decision-log gate.

finding.title: Pairwise covariance diagonal bypasses the 30-obs minimum for short-history names
finding.problem: _pairwise_covariance enforces min_periods=30 for off-diagonal entries (recent.cov(min_periods=30); pairs below the threshold become NaN and are zeroed), but the diagonal is then overwritten by np.fill_diagonal(cov, var) where var = recent.var(axis=0, skipna=True) — computed from as few as 2 observations. A newly-listed name (listing-mask ON: pre-listing rows of raw_returns are NaN, and raw_returns is exactly the risk_source the covariance is estimated from) therefore enters the optimizer as an asset with ZERO covariance to every other name plus a variance estimated from a handful of days. Since raw_returns is un-imputed, foreign-holiday NaNs make the pairwise branch the dominant production path, so this code executes on essentially every rebalance.
finding.scenario: A name lists mid-sample (e.g. GEV 2024-04 or SNDK-type entrants in the 250 universe); 10 trading days later a rebalance fires. The name has a finite LightGBM prediction (fundamental/analyst features exist from listing day; LightGBM tolerates NaN rolling features) and a positive cap-weighted bm weight. In the 126-day window it has 10 valid returns: all its cov entries are zeroed (<30 overlap) and its diagonal is a 10-obs sample variance (standard error ~47% of the true variance). MVO sees an apparently uncorrelated, possibly half-true-vol asset: the quad_form TE constraint dramatically understates its active-risk contribution, so the optimizer can load it toward the 12% OW cap on noise (error maximization). Realized TE and the book composition around every listing event are silently wrong versus a correctly-estimated covariance.
finding.fix: In _pairwise_covariance, apply the same observation minimum to the diagonal: compute counts = recent.count().reindex(recent.columns).to_numpy() and change the var fill to var = np.where((counts >= 30) & np.isfinite(var) & (var > 0), var, np.maximum(np.nan_to_num(var, nan=0.0), fallback_var)) — i.e. names below 30 obs get at least the cross-sectional median (fallback) variance instead of a noisy small-sample one. (Note this removes the understated-variance channel; the zero-correlation diversification magnet for sub-30-obs names remains and is worth a follow-up decision-log entry, e.g. inflating their variance further or pinning them to bm.) This changes certified S0 numbers, so per the project contract it must go through the decision-log/parity gate, not be hotfixed.
